root_cause.text: In `drivers/crypto/ccp/ccp-ops.c:ccp_run_aes_gcm_cmd`, a heap pointer local variable was incorrectly annotated with `__cleanup(kfree)` instead of `__free(kfree)`, causing cleanup to pass the address of the stack variable (`struct ... **`) to `kfree` rather than the `kzalloc`-returned heap pointer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `} *wa __cleanup(kfree) = kzalloc(sizeof *wa, GFP_KERNEL);` to `} *wa __free(kfree) = kzalloc(sizeof(*wa), GFP_KERNEL);`, and the commit/CVE text explicitly states that `__cleanup(kfree)` “will make the address of the local variable, rather than the address returned by kmalloc, passed to kfree directly” leading to “invalid deallocation of stack address.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Switch the temporary work-area allocation to the `__free(kfree)` scoped cleanup helper without changing its automatic lifetime management.
intent_record.what: The local pointer variable `wa` in `ccp_run_aes_gcm_cmd` was changed from using the `__cleanup(kfree)` attribute to `__free(kfree)`, and the allocation size expression was reformatted from `sizeof *wa` to `sizeof(*wa)` in the `kzalloc` call.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the allocated `wa` object is still automatically freed when the variable goes out of scope, so behavior is effectively unchanged; the main effect is adopting the newer scoped cleanup helper macro without altering the allocation or lifetime semantics.

grouping_result.intent: Switch the temporary work-area allocation to the `__free(kfree)` scoped cleanup helper without changing its automatic lifetime management.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause by replacing the incorrect `__cleanup(kfree)` annotation on a heap pointer with `__free(kfree)`, ensuring the allocated pointer itself is freed rather than passing the stack variable’s address to `kfree`.

candidates.rationale: This declaration applies __cleanup(kfree) to a heap pointer local variable. For cleanup attributes, kfree is invoked on the address of the local variable at scope exit, i.e. a pointer-to-pointer on the stack, instead of the kzalloc-returned heap pointer, causing the invalid free described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This local heap pointer declaration uses __cleanup(kfree) on a pointer variable allocated by kzalloc. On scope exit, the cleanup helper passes the address of the local variable to kfree rather than the heap object it points to, resulting in an invalid free of a stack address instead of the allocated work area.
